title: `Tree`: Unexpected `scrollbar_margin_*` and `scroll_bar_*_separation` behavior
body: ### Tested versions - v4.8.dev (8bc207870) ### System information Godot v4.8.dev (8bc207870) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 SUPER (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 63.11 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description In the examples below you can see: - The left margin does not affect the `VScrollBar` in image 1 I would expect all sides of the `ScrollBar` to have equally large gaps. - 2 the h separation property is used to compensate this - 3 we see a negative `H Separation` lets the `Tree`s content go behind the `ScrollBar` but this doesn't affect the title bar background - (1,2,3) The bottom margin not only reduces the `ScrollBar` size but also cuts off the `Tree` content - 4 the margins are still there even when the `ScrollBar` is hidden, but `H Separation` no longer extends the content - Probably mirrored behavior for the `HScrollBar` | 1 | 2 | |:-------------------------:|:-------------------------:| | | | 3 | 4 | | | ### Steps to reproduce Create a `Tree` and test the different settings. You can fill it with content through a `tool` script for example: ```gdscript @tool extends Tree @export_tool_button("build") var build = _generate_tree @export_tool_button("build_big") var build_big = _generate_tree.bind(true) @export_tool_button("clear") var c = clear func _generate_tree(big: bool = false) -> void: clear() set_column_title(0, "Test") for i in range(20 if big else 1): var prop2: TreeItem = create_item() prop2.set_text(0, str(i).repeat(200)) ``` ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
